patches.before: None in an active payload is an env violation on a master port and a DUT violation on a slave port.
patches.after: The None check covers only the K2 identity projection of an accepted or held strobed request. That projection is WE, address and SEL, plus SEL-enabled data lanes when WE=1. None in the projection is an env violation on a master port and a DUT violation on a slave port. Read data lanes and SEL-disabled write lanes carry no identity and are never judged (rule 3.60 qualifies payload, but does not make non-identity lanes meaningful).

patches.before: NOT judged: neither forward order nor side-effect order, within one slave or across slaves.
patches.after: NOT judged: neither forward order nor side-effect order, within one slave or across slaves. Every scoped_pass report must list K5 as an explicit exclusion. A pass never asserts order preservation. This applies in particular to fault/live_order_swap and new_aba/younger_equal_first.

patches.before: If no such entry exists, the response is invented and the hypothesis dies.
patches.after: If no such entry exists, the response is invented and the hypothesis dies, with ONE exception. If the response is an ERR (never an ACK) in row c on master m, and row c shows m holding an unaccepted strobed request (pre i_mcyc[m]&i_mstb[m]&o_mstall[m]), the ERR is tagged possible_starvation_err (unknown). Basis: wbxbar.v header 37-39 says a starved master receives a bus error, but gives no phase, timing or precedence. The tagged ERR retires nothing and creates no entry. The held request stays unaccepted, and a later acceptance of it is a normal new entry. The tag does not claim starvation occurred and carries no timing inference. An ACK in the same situation still has no basis: K6 (inferred) invention applies and the hypothesis dies.

patches.before: normative: exclusivity; inferred: decode ERR and slave-ERR propagation; unknown: timeout/starvation conditions and precedence
patches.after: normative: exclusivity; inferred: decode ERR and slave-ERR propagation; unknown: timeout/starvation conditions and precedence, including ERR on an unaccepted held request (possible_starvation_err, see K6)

patches.before: If pre o_scyc&o_sstb&i_sstall in row c with no reset, row c+1 must have either o_scyc=0, or o_sstb=1 with an identical payload.
patches.after: If pre o_scyc&o_sstb&i_sstall holds in row c with no reset, row c+1 must have either o_scyc=0, or o_sstb=1 with an identical K2 identity projection. The projection is WE, address and SEL, plus SEL-enabled data lanes when WE=1. Read data and SEL-disabled write lanes may change.

inferred (reading of WB 3.1.2 and rule 3.30 applied to the DUT's slave role toward each master; the rule text constrains response to slave signals while CYC is negated, and this design reads that as forbidding ACK/ERR emission)

patches.before: o_mack/o_merr[m] in row c with pre i_mcyc[m]=0 in both rows c-1 and c is a dut_violation.
patches.after: o_mack/o_merr[m] in row c with pre i_mcyc[m]=0 in both rows c-1 and c is a dut_violation (inferred, K13). No DUT response latency is derived from OPT_DBLBUFFER or any other option name; the one-row allowance follows only from the same-edge observability argument below. A response with CYC low is not an active-cycle retirement, so K6 is not cited as an independent basis for it.

patches.before: master_epoch[m] increments on every CYC 1->0. reset_epoch increments per reset. Both are arbitrary-precision in the checker. If a bounded implementation is used, overflow triggers the resource-exhaustion path.
patches.after: master_epoch[m] increments on every CYC 1->0, and reset_epoch increments per reset. The association-free projection counters are also arbitrary-precision in the checker: per-identity master and slave counts, per-slave forwards and responses, and per-master acceptances and responses in the current CYC. None of them is ever pruned or truncated when hypothesis resources are exhausted, so the projections stay exact and sound. If a bounded implementation is used and any counter would overflow, that counter's projection becomes unresolved_on_counter_limit(row) for the rest of the reset epoch. It never wraps or saturates into a verdict.

Time-bounded. Let e be the first row with an env violation. (1) A DUT violation whose complete evidence lies in rows < e stays dut_violation; a later invalid input cannot erase it. (2) A DUT violation evidenced in row e itself, as a same-edge mixed fault, is reported as mixed_same_edge(dut_candidate, env) with the explicit note that no public ordering exists. It is unresolved for the DUT, unless the DUT check depends only on pins and on inputs from rows < e. (3) Every judgment needing rows >= e is input_or_scope_invalid. A clause whose evidence lies wholly before e may still be reported as prefix_scoped_pass, bounded to rows < e. (4) Trace aggregate: dut_violation if (1) applies, else input_or_scope_invalid if e exists, else violation > unresolved > pass. Both the env record and any prefix verdict are always listed.

patches.before: No pruning and no branch selection. For the remainder of the current reset epoch, record unresolved_on_limit(row, sizes) and suspend all association-dependent judgments for all masters: K4 per-candidate consumption, K6, K7, K8 attribution, K9 tags and K12.
patches.after: No pruning and no branch selection. For the remainder of the current reset epoch, record unresolved_on_limit(row, sizes) and suspend all association-dependent judgments for all masters: K4 per-candidate consumption, K6, K7, K8 attribution, K9 tags and K12. Violations recorded before the exhaustion row stay final. Mandatory metric for each run and each clause: suspended_rows, total_rows, the suspended fraction, and the exhaustion rows and sizes. A clause suspended in any row may never be reported scoped_pass; the best it can be is unresolved(suspended). The report also states the effective checked scope in rows.

patches.before: Per-master responses in current CYC <= acceptances in current CYC
patches.after: Per-master ACKs in current CYC <= acceptances in current CYC. ERRs in the same CYC are counted against acceptances, except an ERR that meets the K6 possible_starvation_err condition. Such an ERR is counted separately and tagged unknown.

Trace/RTL mutation control, not a property edit. Use a reachable stimulus in which X is accepted once and the mutated DUT forwards X twice (the fault/duplicate_consumed_identity pattern). It must fail, and a cover must reach the second forward. A property-harness sanity mutation, such as the trivial strict-< form, may be logged only as a harness check; it is never evidence of transaction sensitivity.

patches.before: A monitor mutated to bind the younger read's data must report empty H on a reachable cover.
patches.after: DUT/trace mutation: retirement data swapped across cross-slave reads (the cross_slave/wrong_retirement_data pattern) must drive the unmutated monitor to empty H, on a reachable cover with both forwards and both slave ACKs. A monitor-mutation run is labeled harness-only.

rationale:
Unaccepted held-request ERR vs ACK: the header documents a starvation bus error but gives no phase or timing. An ERR during a held, stalled request is therefore tagged unknown and not proven starvation. An ACK there has no source and remains invention. The post-exhaustion invariant is revised to match.

Precedence is time-bounded: earlier DUT violations persist, later judgments are invalid, and same-edge mixed faults are explicitly unordered.

None checks and stall-hold checks are restricted to the identity projection.

K13 is reclassified as inferred, with no latency inferred from OPT_DBLBUFFER. stale_after_reset no longer cites K6 for a CYC-low response.

Projection counters are exact and never pruned, so they stay sound after hypothesis exhaustion; counter overflow becomes unresolved, never a verdict. Suspended scope is measured, and scoped_pass is forbidden on any suspended clause.

K5 is excluded in every pass.

False controls are now DUT/trace mutations with covers; harness edits are labeled harness-only.

Review F6 is rejected: the exact rows and ledger give accepts at 6, 10 and 14, the forward at 16, the slave ACK at 17 and the master ACK at 18. The existing cycle-18 citation stands unchanged.

No results, RTL or experiments are claimed, and budgets are unchanged.
